structured.approach: This step ran in check mode because the TRD does not flag a platform-level change (record:intake). I read the approved TRD, the feature's org.architecture override, the base org/org.architecture.md and the decision log. I went through each statement in the platform documents: the four-repository flow, the runtimes, the signature rule, the return-shape rule, the JSON money and date rule, the no-database/no-network rule for ap_aging, tenancy and security, the LLM provider and the decisions. For each one I asked whether the TRD changes it. I then looked at the findings that come close to platform level (TQ-3 transport, the vendor key, new public functions, the bucket_for and formatAmount conflicts, and the LLM data flow) and wrote down what would make the action necessary. I wrote one check record and changed no code, configuration or architecture document. I did not use any connector because the inputs held every fact I needed.

claims.text: The step runs as a check because its condition was not met: the TRD does not flag a platform-level change.

The platform architecture describes four repositories in one flow: ap_pipeline, ap_forecast, ap_aging and ap_portal. ap_pipeline, ap_forecast and ap_aging run on Python 3.9 and ap_portal on Node.js 22 CommonJS. The rule is to keep every existing signature and add new functions.
The TRD changes only the same four repositories and adds no new repository or service (components C-1 to C-10).

Only two existing functions change, both additively: to_model keeps its signature and return shape and gains a paid_date record key, and build_explanation_request gains risk=None as its last parameter. The TRD's own validation records the signature rule as Pass.
The new CT-1 contract sends amount as a two-decimal string and has no date field. This applies the existing platform rule for JSON between services.

The base platform document describes ap_aging as a pure Python 3.9 library with no database, no network and no secrets, and says existing signatures and return shapes must not change. The TRD adds no storage, schema migration or persistent data, and keeps aging_buckets, days_past_due and bucket_for unchanged.
Finance posting, authentication, tenancy, payment execution and the LLM provider or model are explicitly not affected, and the risk tier is T2.
New code is consistent with D-2026-031, D-2026-044 and D-2026-050.

Ownership of serialisation and transport between ap_aging and ap_portal is still open (TQ-3). If the answer introduces a new service or transport layer, that would be a platform-level change and DES-01 should be re-run.
Conclusion: no platform architecture update is needed now. All changes are additive functions plus one feature-level contract that follows the existing JSON rule.

open_questions: Should org.architecture's function lists be updated to name the new public functions (delays_by_vendor, vendor_risk, overdue_with_risk, overdue_rows_to_json, renderOverdueRisk) once FEAT-ZD-48600 is released? This is documentation upkeep, not an architecture change.
The base org/org.architecture.md covers ap_aging only, while the feature override covers the four-repository flow. Should the base document be widened to the four-repository flow?
structured.summary: DES-01 check for FEAT-ZD-48600: no platform architecture update is needed now. The approved TRD keeps the four-repository flow, the runtimes, every existing signature and return shape, the JSON rule for amounts and dates, the no-database/no-network property of ap_aging, the LLM provider, and tenancy and security unchanged. Every change is an additive function, plus one feature-level contract (CT-1) that follows the existing JSON rule. The check record at checks/DES-01_feat.platform_update.md lists the evidence for each platform statement and five near-platform findings. It also lists six triggers that would require a full DES-01 run, chiefly a new transport layer coming out of TQ-3 or any change to an existing signature or return shape.
